Optional. For example: only while the flashlight is on, only on your home Wi-Fi, or only at night.

Give one app its own assignments: inside it they replace In Apps' and Anywhere's for the same trigger, everywhere else nothing changes.
A menu pops up a list of actions to choose from. Assign it to a trigger from the action picker's Menus category. Swipe left on a menu to delete it.
A menu pops up a list of actions to choose from. Make one, then assign it to a trigger from the action picker.
Name shown at the top of the menu
Tap a profile to switch to it or export it; swipe left to delete it. Switching saves your current setup into the active profile first, so nothing is lost.
Export makes a file you can send with AirDrop, Messages or Files. Import replaces your current setup after showing what it contains.
Clears every assignment, menu and setting, and turns off Allow API (Replace Button Actions goes back on). Saved profiles are kept.
Every assignment, menu and setting is cleared. Saved profiles are kept.
Saves your current assignments, menus and settings. An existing profile with this name is replaced.

text: On: an assigned press runs instead of the button's own action. Off: both run. Waking, Emergency SOS and force restart always work.
A banner names what just ran. Haptic Feedback is a small tap; it follows iOS's System Haptics setting.
Respring, Restart and Power Off ask before they run, from a trigger or from Run Now. Safe Mode never asks, so it always works when a tweak gets stuck.
On: Shortcuts run like Back Tap runs them, without opening the app. Off: the Shortcuts app opens.
Triggr ignores triggers while one of these apps is open, like a game that uses the volume buttons.
Lets the status bar's single-tap triggers run. Double Tap and Hold always work.
Experimental on Face ID iPhones, so it starts off: a tap at the top can begin pulling down Control Center. Double Tap and Hold always work.
Apps and Shortcuts always wait for you to unlock. With this on, shell commands wait too.
Lets other tweaks and the triggr command run your triggers and built-in actions (never commands or apps). Leave off unless you use it.
Save and switch setups, share them as a file, or reset Triggr to its defaults.
Nothing changes until you assign something. A button with nothing assigned keeps doing its normal thing.
A button press, a gesture, or something that happens, like plugging in the charger. Use Add a Trigger on the main page.
One action, or several that run in order.
It works right away. No respring.
In Your Setup, swipe right on a trigger, or touch and hold it, and choose Run Now. Its actions run straight away.
Remove one, or bring it back
Swipe left on a trigger in Your Setup to remove it. An Undo button shows at the top right for a few seconds and brings it back with its actions and Only If conditions.
Some triggers only appear on iPhones that have that button or sensor.
Home, Lock (Side), Volume, Mute switch, Action button, Touch ID and the headset button: single, double and triple presses, holds, Volume Up then Down, and Lock + Volume together.
Status bar taps and swipes, slides in from the screen edges, Home Screen pinches and icon flicks, taps and swipes with two to five fingers inside apps, the Lock Screen clock and the home bar.
Shaking the phone, and covering or waving over the sensor by the earpiece.
Charger, headphones, CarPlay, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Low Power Mode, locking and unlocking, calls, music, notifications, apps opening, a time of day, and sunrise or sunset.
Turn the flashlight, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Do Not Disturb, Dark Mode, Low Power Mode and more on, off, or the other way round.
Play, pause and skip, volume, AirPlay, and steps of brightness, volume or flashlight brightness.
Open Camera already recording video, or start a new voice memo. Run it again to stop and save.
Open any app, Settings page or link, or run one of your Shortcuts without the Shortcuts app opening.
Show a message or banner, say the time or battery level out loud, or run a shell command.
Actions from tweaks that support Triggr, and the old Activator actions many tweaks still include.
Run only when something is true: on your home Wi-Fi, charging, between certain times, while the flashlight is on, and more. Otherwise the trigger does its normal thing.
Pick more than one action to run them in order. Order, Pauses & If adds waits between them and If / Otherwise steps.
Give the same trigger a different action on the Home Screen, inside apps, on the Lock Screen, or in one app only.
A list of actions that pops up so you can pick one, all from a single trigger.
Set these up with Add a Trigger on the main page.
A button press, a swipe, or something that happens, like plugging in your charger.
Turn on the flashlight, open an app or run a shortcut. Pick a few and they run in order.
Swipe right on a trigger, or hold it, to run it without pressing anything.
Triggr reacts only to the triggers you add. Everything else works as usual.
For one place only (Home Screen, apps, Lock Screen), open that place above instead.
Tap one to change it. Swipe right or hold it to run it now, swipe left to remove it.
Nothing set up yet. Add a Trigger to start, or open the Guide to see what Triggr can do.
SpringBoard crashed while Triggr was handling the Action button, so the button went back to iOS. It tries again after the next Triggr update. Your other triggers still work.
Most things belong in Anywhere. Use a place when a trigger should do something different there.
Start and end, 24-hour, e.g. 22:00-06:00 (overnight is fine)
Wait this many seconds, then run only if the opposite didn't happen meanwhile (e.g. you didn't rejoin the network).
Runs instead of going Home (or waking) wherever this assignment applies. To go Home as well, add Go to Home Screen.
Runs instead of the App Switcher. To open it as well, add App Switcher.
Runs instead of Reachability (the light double tap). To keep it, add Reachability.
Runs instead of the Accessibility Shortcut, and double presses wait a moment to see if a third follows.
Runs instead of Siri. To keep Siri, add Siri.
Runs instead of turning the volume up. To change it as well, add Volume Up (Media).
Runs instead of turning the volume down. To change it as well, add Volume Down (Media).
Hold one volume button and press the other. The second button won't change the volume; the first may still move it one step.
Both volume buttons held for 0.5 s. The second button won't change the volume; the first may still move it one step.
Runs instead of locking while the screen is on. To lock as well, add Sleep.
Single presses wait a moment to see if another follows.
Single and double presses wait a moment to see if another follows.
Runs instead of the power-off slider. To show it as well, add Power Off Slider.

The lock press won't lock and Volume Up won't change the volume if it's pressed second. Without a Home button it also runs instead of the screenshot; to take it as well, add Take Screenshot. With Up Hold assigned too, it runs when you let go.
The lock press won't lock and Volume Down won't change the volume if it's pressed second. With Down Hold assigned too, it runs when you let go.
Runs after half a second, alongside iOS: keep holding and the power-off slider and Emergency SOS appear as usual.
Runs instead of muting, so the ringer stays on. To mute as well, add Mute On (Switches).
Runs instead of unmuting, so the ringer stays off. To unmute as well, add Mute Off (Switches).
Runs instead of muting or unmuting. To change it as well, add Toggle Mute (Switches).
Runs alongside the normal press, which still goes Home.
Hold one volume button and press the other. Both still change the volume.
Both volume buttons held for 0.5 s. Both still change the volume.
Runs alongside every press, which still locks.
Runs after the presses stop; each press still locks or wakes.
Runs alongside the buttons, which still lock and change the volume (and take the screenshot without a Home button).
Runs alongside the buttons, which still lock and change the volume.
Runs alongside the switch, which still mutes.
Runs alongside the switch, which still unmutes.
Runs alongside the switch, which still mutes and unmutes.
To run instead, turn on Replace Button Actions in Options.
A hold that's released before Siri appears.
Runs after holding for 0.5 s; the volume still changes by one step.
A swipe to the next page that starts on an icon runs this instead. Swipe between icons to change pages.
A swipe to the previous page that starts on an icon runs this instead. Swipe between icons to change pages.
A swipe down for Search that starts on an icon runs this instead.
Press Up, then Down, quickly. Up presses wait 0.4 s for Down. Runs alongside the two presses.
Press Down, then Up, quickly. Down presses wait 0.4 s for Up. Runs alongside the two presses.
Flip the switch and back within 0.8 s. Runs alongside, so the ringer ends where it started.
On iOS 18 this is also Type to Siri when that's on; Triggr's action runs instead.
Comes before iOS's hold to change the wallpaper, which still works off the clock.
Takes the place of the swipe back many apps use. The two-finger version leaves it alone.
While assigned, that third of the bottom edge stops opening Control Center or going Home (portrait only).
A fast, straight flick along the edge, mid-screen. A fast flick from the edge can set it off, so pick something harmless.
That third of the top edge stops opening Notification Center or Control Center while assigned.
Clashes with apps that zoom (Photos, Safari, Maps).
Also iOS's copy gesture in text, so best in apps without typing.
Also iOS's paste gesture in text, so best in apps without typing.
Cover the sensor for under half a second.
With Live Voicemail on, a call that goes to voicemail counts too.
Once per new song, including the first after a pause.
Runs once a day if the phone is on.
Runs at this time while Triggr is running. iOS can delay timers while the phone sleeps; if it's more than 5 minutes late, it's skipped.
Runs once when the level passes this percentage, not on every change.
If Double Tap is also assigned, single taps wait a moment to see if a second follows.
If Left Double Tap (or Double Tap) is also assigned, single taps wait a moment to see if a second follows.
If Right Double Tap (or Double Tap) is also assigned, single taps wait a moment to see if a second follows.
Respring and Safe Mode restart SpringBoard, so actions after them won't run. Keep them last.
Safe Mode restarts SpringBoard with no tweaks, Triggr included, until you tap Dismiss on the Safe Mode screen.
Nothing runs after a restart or power off. Keep it last.
This restarts or powers off the phone as soon as the trigger fires, without asking. The jailbreak stays off until you run Dopamine again.
%@ and %@ change the same switch, so only the last one sticks.
%@ and %@ can't open at the same time. Add a pause between them in Order, Pauses & If.
Light Double Tap: touch the sensor twice without clicking. Finger Match works on the Lock Screen only.
Up, then Down is two quick presses; it runs as the second button goes down. While one is assigned, a single press waits a moment for the other button.
Press the lock button and a volume button together. Holds run after half a second; keep holding and iOS's power-off slider still appears.
Hold is what iOS uses for the button's own action. Assign Hold to replace it; Press and Double Press are extra.
Toggled Twice: flip it and back quickly; it runs on the flip back. While it's assigned, a single flip waits a moment.
Double tap the line at the bottom, inside apps. Single taps still work.
Gestures that start on the big Lock Screen clock. The rest of the Lock Screen is unchanged.
The button on wired headphones. Hold replaces Siri while it's assigned.
Left and Right are each half of the bar. A single tap still scrolls to the top.
A quick flick that starts on an app or folder icon.
Slide from the very edge of the screen. An assigned part of an edge stops doing its iOS gesture there, so open a trigger to see what it takes over.
On an empty part of a Home Screen page, not on an icon.
Inside apps. The app still sees the gesture too, so pick ones it doesn't use; two- and three-finger taps and swipes are safest.
Uses iOS's own shake detection, so no extra battery.
Taking out an AirPod can count as Headphones Disconnected.
Worked out from the location iOS already has. No tracking.
Phone, FaceTime and other calling apps.
Any notification. Triggr only sees which app sent it. For one app, use Custom Events.
Any app in Now Playing: Music, Spotify, YouTube, podcasts…
The sensor by the earpiece. It stays on while the screen is on (a little battery). Wave is a quick cover; with Wave assigned, Cover waits half a second.
Runs after the change. Control Center's Wi-Fi button only leaves the network; Wi-Fi stays on.
%lu assignments, %lu menus, %lu shell commands, %lu URLs or Shortcuts.
Seconds to wait before the next action (0.1–%g).
Raise brightness by this much each time, 1–50 % (10 is a good step)
Lower brightness by this much each time, 1–50 % (10 is a good step)
Any URL or URL scheme, e.g. https://…, tel:… or music://
Battery level, 1–100 %. Runs once when the level climbs past it; 100 means fully charged.
Battery level, 1–100 %. Runs once when the level falls past it.
Network name (SSID), as shown in Settings → Wi-Fi
Device name, as shown in Settings → Bluetooth

Home, App Switcher, Control Center, Spotlight, Siri, screenshots, lock, respring, restart and more. Triggr asks before it resprings, restarts or turns off your iPhone. Turn that off in Options → Ask Before Restarting.
Save your whole setup, switch between setups, or share it as a file. In Options → Profiles, Sharing & Reset.
Volume Up → Flashlight Brighter and Volume Down → Flashlight Dimmer, each Only If the flashlight is on. When it's off, the buttons change the volume as usual.
Hold both volume buttons → Record Video.
Hold Volume Up → Next Track, hold Volume Down → Previous Track. Short presses still change the volume.
Double-tap the status bar → Lock Device.
Joined your home Wi-Fi → turn Low Power Mode off and open your music app.
Runs instead of the button's own action (Settings → Action Button).
